title: Sherpa Tensing — Descent Ten: Past Perfect Passive (B2)
description: By the time you got there, it was already over — and nobody in the sentence did it. This is the tense of arriving too late, told from the point of view of…

hero.lede: By the time you got there, it was already over — and nobody in the sentence did it. This is the tense of arriving too late, told from the point of view of the thing it happened to.

sections.label: Descent briefing
sections.title: When to use it
sections.lead: The passive is not a different tense. It is the past perfect with the doer let go — and the reason you let them go is always one of these six.

cards.head: You do not know who
cards.body: Nobody can tell you the doer, so the sentence does without one.
cards.ex: "The safe had been emptied before the police arrived."

cards.head: The doer does not matter
cards.body: The event is the news; who did it is a footnote.

cards.head: The doer is obvious
cards.body: Saying it would be a waste of everyone's time.

cards.head: You would rather not say
cards.body: The passive is how English removes a person from a sentence.
cards.ex: "The decision had been taken long before the meeting."

cards.head: Putting the important thing first
cards.body: Whatever you put at the front is what the sentence is about.

cards.head: Putting the doer back with by
cards.body: When the doer is the point, it goes at the end.
cards.ex: "The report had been written by an intern."

cards.head: Negative
cards.body: the not goes after the first auxiliary

cards.head: Questions
cards.body: the first auxiliary moves to the front

charts.head: Turning an active sentence around
charts.note: Three moves, always the same: the object comes to the front, the verb becomes had been + participle, and the old subject either disappears or goes to the back behind by. Only the middle step changes from camp to camp.

head: Active
Passive
What moved
rows: An intern had written the report.
The report had been written by an intern.
The intern stayed, at the end.
They had deleted all the files.
All the files had been deleted.

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: The shortest chart on the descent. Had been is the same for everybody — no was and were, no third-person -s — and the participle never moves.

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this one is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: Without the participle you have written an adjective: the safe simply had nothing in it.
Yesterday the safe had been emptied.
With no second past event to stand behind, the past simple passive is the tense.

charts.note: Neither is better. The question is only what the sentence is about — because whatever you put at the front is what the reader will think it is about.

head: Question
Passive
Active
rows:
The thing it happens to.
"The safe had been emptied."

The one who does it.
"Someone had emptied the safe."
Often not — and you do not need to.
Yes, and you are naming them.
At the end with by, or nowhere at all.
At the front, as the subject.
Longer by two or three words.
Usually shorter. Prefer it when both work.

charts.example: Two past moments, and the passive removes the person from the earlier one. By the time we got there the files had been deleted tells you the deletion came first and refuses to say who did it — which, in that particular sentence, is usually the whole story.

sections.label: Trail markers
sections.title: Signal words

signals.head: Verbs with no passive at all

sections.example: The test for whether a verb can go passive: does it take an object? They built it has one, so it turns. It happened has none, so it cannot.

sections.title: The event, and the doer you dropped

diagram.intro: The block is the same block as the ascent, lit from above instead of fading into the dark — because the tense has not changed, only the light. Inside it sits a dashed box: the doer. It is drawn inside the event rather than beside it because the doer is not a moment in time, it is a part of the sentence — and it is dashed because most of the time nobody says it. Click either to see it in a sentence.

panels.head: The doer — optional, and usually gone
items: … and nobody could say by whom.

quiz.prompt: The safe _____ before the police arrived. (empty)
quiz.explain: Had + been + participle. Had been empty would only describe its state.

quiz.hint: A state reaching a past moment.
quiz.explain: For months measured back from a past moment takes the past perfect passive.
Had been is the same for every subject.

quiz.prompt: _____ the room _____ before you got there? (clean)

quiz.explain: Write / wrote / written, and the doer behind by.

quiz.hint: Is there a second past event?
quiz.explain: With nothing for it to be earlier than, the past simple passive is right.
Before that evening gives the second past moment the past perfect needs.
Had been told. Tell / told / told.

quiz.prompt: The decision _____ long before the meeting. (take)
quiz.explain: Take / took / taken — and notice the meeting was for show.

quiz.hint: By then sets the past moment.
quiz.explain: By then needs a moment to measure back from, so the past perfect passive.

quiz.prompt: We _____ to a different floor before the audit. (move)
quiz.explain: Had been moved says it happened to us, earlier than the audit.
Happen takes no object, so it has no passive.

quiz.prompt: The gate _____ , so we climbed over. (lock)
quiz.explain: Had been locked: already done by the time we got there.

results: Clean run. You can turn a sentence around and you know when the doer is worth keeping.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at the active version before you go on.
Good first attempt. The auxiliary chain is the part to read again.
